name: The elopement and assassination
description: The [[Prince of Miurna]] and the [[Sultana of Caryes]] eloped and were assassinated. Given the enmity between the [[group/realm-aphemenosta|Rock of Aphemenosta]] and Miurna, the elopement was beyond scandalous. Folk stories give them an infant, the [[Lost Heir]], who escaped; every court holds that the Prince died childless or that any child died with him. Some, particularly in the Order, believe the [[Engineers]] instigated it to stop a consolidation of power into a pan-continental personal union.

name: The Madness of Cargal IV
description: The loss of his eldest son, the [[Prince of Miurna]], drove [[Cargal IV]] mad. He died with the succession unsettled.

name: The Union of the Kingdoms breaks apart
description:
After the death of [[Cargal IV]] the court fragmented and the [[Union of the Kingdoms]] split apart. His younger sons contested the throne. [[Ceoin Miurna]] had precedence by primogeniture, but [[Alba Miurna]], widely seen as the more effective statesman, won the backing of most of the elders of the court and of the late king's brother, [[Lord Read of the Leantain Reach]]. With the Union's wealth centred in Miurna, and long resentment of the court's bias to the wealthier East, the Western kingdoms backed Ceoin's natural claim, and his argument that the Union should have many voices, in return for his moving his putative throne to the West. Alba claimed the throne of the Union in the capital, but his rule did not meaningfully reach the West, where fealty was privately sworn to Ceoin.

A long and contentious period followed. Skirmishes between lords' retinues, levies and town militias pocked the land, and free companies with no war to be paid for roamed and raided, disowned by both sides. Only the economic cost of open hostility kept the factions on a narrow path of backchannel politics and trade, and a fragile stability held until the [[Treaty of Sinte]].

name: The Treaty of Sinte
description: Signed by [[Ceoin Miurna]] and [[Alba Miurna]]. It gave the Western realms to Ceoin and kept the historical and commercial heart of Miurna for Alba. To keep a balance both could accept, neither brother would rule [[group/realm-godrastan|Godrastan]], the expansive third kingdom, an exclave to the East: the elders of the old court would, and it would stay neutral. That was a boon for Alba, as the elders had been his chief advocates regardless. Ceoin's gain was recognition: the Western kingdoms, united under the banner of Leantis, became a kingdom in their own right, free to make alliances and trade abroad, no longer a contested region within Alba's Union. The other states of the [[Greater Lands]] could at last deal openly with all three kingdoms.

name: The Invasion of Leantis
description: The opening of the [[Brotherly War]], almost a decade after the [[Treaty of Sinte]]: [[Alba Miurna|Alba]]'s Miurnan army stormed across the poorer kingdom. Leantis reacted in time to stop it short of [[Ceoin Miurna|Ceoin]]'s capital, and contained the Miurnans long enough to come to a war footing, set up its own supply and mount a counter-offensive. The empty hinterland that slowed the advance hurt the invader more than the defender: an army that lives off the land it crosses goes hungry in sparse country.

name: The Brotherly War
description:
The war between [[Alba Miurna|Alba]]'s Miurna and [[Ceoin Miurna|Ceoin]]'s Leantis, opened by the [[Invasion of Leantis]]. Miurna was better resourced, but Ceoin's home ground and native support balanced the scales; near the southern coast, where Leantis was strongest, it pushed into Miurna, splitting the Miurnan army in response. In the sparse hinterlands of both kingdoms the war became a patchwork of campaigns for key settlements, towns, routes and resources: a bitter stalemate of interlocking garrisons, grinding the middle of the continent to a standstill. Each garrison sold protection to the villages around it, so holding land came to mean collecting from it.

On paper the borders stayed as they had been before the war, and for the most part taxes and trade flowed to the established capitals, if at all, where they could dodge captured enclaves and roving columns. But Miurna clawed back ever larger tracts in a war of attrition, and the war gradually crippled Leantis's economy.

Neighbouring states largely stayed formally neutral, but the so-called [[Golden Axis]] of Miurna, [[group/realm-godrastan|Godrastan]], [[group/realm-high-marks|the High Marks]] and certain of [[the Nine States]] was a geopolitical faction warmer to Miurna than to Leantis. Leantis had no sincere allies, only sympathetic words.

name: Caryes unites with Sevine
description: Caryes negotiates a union with the Principality of Sevine, which owed fealty to the Sultana, to keep her personal union from breaking up.

name: The Order of the White Raven is founded
description: Founded at the Raven of Carrowmore public house in Linos.

name: The Sultan withdraws to the Harem
description: A mortal sickness drove [[Caruman II]] from his offices to his chamber in [[the Harem]], where none but his wives could follow. Many feared his death without a legitimate heir, and with none possible, would plunge [[group/realm-astina|Astina]] into turmoil, leaving it open to powerful neighbours and erstwhile friends who would plunder its riches and rewrite its treaties. Instead, it was announced, his health stabilised at death's door, and the Harem became the voice of his will. Whether or when he died, he has not been allowed to.

name: The Cutting of the Prime Reach
description: The [[Engineers]]' first canal in the [[Greater Lands]], cut across [[group/realm-zintar|Zintar]] from the [[Inner Sea]] to the [[Bay of Brael]]. Ostensibly a logical shortening of the [[Freti]]; but the political economics were naked, for it bypassed [[group/realm-astina|Astina]] and ended its hold on the [[Nine States]]' sea access to the Gulf. Zintar ceded the strip in a commercial deal, for years of Engineer funding and political support; its own ships may pass the canal at a price little more than the cost of the Freti, for a fraction of the time. The canal and the strip on either side became the territory of the [[Committee Exterior]]. Astina's loss of trade was no concern of the Engineers, and Astina had no right to that trade to claim: a monopoly of the route was never a title to it.

name: The Coming (an Teacht)
description: The arrival on [[Inis Mara]] of the forebears of the [[Engineers]], who found it sparsely peopled: year 0 of the reckoning they still keep, *bliain ón Teacht* (óT, years since the Coming). The present day is **812 óT**. Of where they came from, and why, their histories say nothing: the Engineers keep their own past in a shroud, even from themselves.

name: The spread through the islands
description: From [[Inis Mara]] the newcomers, and the farming they brought, spread to [[Inis Tíre]] and the other islands of what are now the [[Lands of the Engineers]].

name: Turned back from Zintar
description: Pushing on across the narrow crossing to the land that is now [[group/realm-zintar|Zintar]], the islanders met resistance, and fell back. The strait became an impenetrable moat against a continent they feared, and for generations the islands kept to themselves.

name: The Empire of the Sun strikes Inis Mara
description: As the [[Empire of the Sun]] grew into a transcontinental power, the first northern land it struck was [[Inis Mara]]: a brutal incursion into a mostly peaceful society. The islanders fell back to their strongholds, and at last to [[Ephe]].

name: The Siege of Ephe
description: The Empire besieged [[Ephe]] by land and sea, and the city survived behind its walls and the moat its people dug about them, the [[Orbital]], thanks to [[group/inis-tire-scholars|a scholarly society of Inis Tíre]], which broke the blockade by sea to bring a secret new craft into the city: lens-making. Under the bright subtropical sun the defenders fashioned lenses and materials to burn and terrify the besiegers.

name: The siege of Ephe is broken
description: Ships came from [[Inis Tíre]] carrying gunpowder better than the Empire's, and broke the siege; the Empire's forces withdrew. The people of [[Inis Mara]] had been decimated.

name: Ore found in Inis Tíre
description: The discovery of ores in a corner of [[Inis Tíre]] gave a boon to a research effort already under way, driven by the wars: defensive and practical inventions kept appearing, and industrial processes kept improving.

name: The Empire's returns
description: The [[Empire of the Sun]] came back to [[Inis Mara]] and [[Inis Tíre]] more than once, and Inis Mara was scoured each time. Each time, too, the islanders were better able to defeat its superior numbers with what they had made since.

name: The Division of Inis Mara
description: The islanders' greatest innovation was diplomatic. Rather than fight for [[Inis Mara]] again, they granted the [[Empire of the Sun]], and the powers of the northern continent, rights to administer it, all but the stronghold city of [[Ephe]] and its surrounds. An invasion of Inis Mara became an invasion of all those lands, and made little sense to an Empire that had land granted to it already, which it would not take up. The grants are the origin of the island's nominal provinces today: [[Beth]], [[Fern]] and [[Luis]].
